Issued at 255 AM EDT Tue Aug 18 2026

Today-Tonight...Surface high pressure will remain just south of 
the Florida peninsula today, allowing for the continued spread 
southward of a moist air mass. Westerly flow prevails both at the 
surface and aloft, resulting in a delayed development of the east 
coast sea breeze. The sea breeze will struggle to push inland, 
with guidance suggesting it should move just past the I-95 
corridor. With the moist air mass overhead causing PWATs to exceed
2" areawide, a return of scattered shower and storm chances is 
anticipated across east central Florida today, with timing following
the diurnal pattern driven by the sea breezes. Activity will 
increase this afternoon, with westerly flow aloft supporting 
offshore-moving showers and storms through late afternoon into 
the evening hours. Sufficient instability from daytime heating and
modest low-level lapse rates supporting vertical growth, dry air 
above 800 mb enhancing downdraft potential, and PWATs exceeding 2"
areawide will support isolated strong storm development across 
the area today. Storm hazards will include frequent lightning 
strikes, wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph, and heavy downpours with the 
potential for quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3" in some spots. 
Minor, localized flooding cannot be ruled out, especially along 
the coast. There is a low chance for some broad rotation as well 
along the sea breeze, with a brief funnel cloud or two not able to
be fully ruled out. Activity wanes into the evening and overnight
hours across the peninsula, with a return of prevailing light 
westerly flow and mostly dry conditions.

Hot conditions will persist across east central Florida today, 
with mostly clear skies through the morning hours supporting 
effective daytime heating. Afternoon highs will continue to climb 
into the mid 90s areawide, remaining above normal values. Humid 
conditions in addition to the highs will result in peak heat 
indices of 108F to 112F, with another Heat Advisory issued across 
all ten east central Florida counties between 10 AM and 8 PM. 
Residents and visitors alike are encouraged to practice heat 
safety, remain adequately hydrated, and avoid spending extended 
periods of time in the heat. Limited relief overnight from the 
muggy conditions, with lows only falling into the mid 70s to low 
80s.

Wednesday-Monday...An active pattern will continue across east 
central Florida through this week and into early next week. Mid-
level ridging will weaken across the Florida peninsula, with 
guidance now favoring a mid-level low developing across the Gulf 
and lifting across north Florida mid to late week. This low would 
be absorbed by a trough digging southward across the eastern US 
this weekend. At the surface, this mid-level pattern would support
persistent increasing moisture locally, with a series of decaying
frontal boundaries anticipated to approach Florida through late 
this week while broad high pressure remains situated across the 
Gulf. Locally, west to southwest winds are forecast to continue 
areawide, with daytime heating supporting the development of the 
east coast sea breeze each day. The push inland during the 
afternoon hours will result in winds becoming more south to 
southeasterly behind it, with westerly winds aloft preventing too 
much intrusion inland. Combined with the moist air mass in place, 
a diurnal pattern of showers and storms will persist, with 
development driven primarily by the sea breezes each day. Rain 
and storm chances will remain near normal (40-60%) through the
period, with storm hazards including lightning strikes, gusty 
winds, and heavy downpours that have the potential to produce 
minor, localized flooding in some spots. With steering flow 
remaining out of the west, activity will push offshore through the
afternoon and evening hours each day, with mostly dry conditions 
anticipated across the peninsula through the overnight hours.

Temperatures are forecast to remain above normal over the next 
couple of days, though the persistent moist pattern will lead to a
trend closer to normal late this week and into the weekend. The 
heat will still remain a concern through this week as peak heat 
indices climb well into triple digits, with continued support from
guidance that some locations across east central Florida may near
and even exceed Heat Advisory thresholds. This will continue to 
be closely monitored and additional heat products will be issued 
as needed.
